chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah said: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated to them from Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Indeed, in the book of Ali (peace be upon him): 'That the paternal aunt is in the position of the father, and the maternal aunt is in the position of the mother, and the daughter of the brother is in the position of the brother, and every relative of kin is in the position of the kinship through which they are connected, unless there is an heir closer to the deceased than them, in which case they are excluded.'

key_terms.بِنْتَ اَلْأَخِ: Daughter of the brother (paternal or maternal)

ai.seo_question: How do aunts and cousins inherit according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* articulates the Shia jurisprudential principle of *tashib* (residuary inheritance), where aunts and cousins inherit as substitutes for their respective male counterparts (father and brother). It clarifies that while these relatives are treated as primary heirs in the absence of closer lines, they are subject to the rule of *hujb* (exclusion) if a closer heir, such as a son or father, exists. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the Quranic text's allowance for collateral inheritance, distinguishing it from some Sunni schools that may limit or exclude aunts in the presence of certain male heirs.
